Faceless TikTok Marketing: Slideshows, Clipping, Brain Rot & Screen Recs

& how to create each one just like the most viral TikTok consumer apps did it Hey there! Today’s edition is Part 1 of a…

SGE Team

•

March 13, 2025

•

7 min read

Save for later

& how to create each one just like the most viral TikTok consumer apps did it

Hey there!

Today’s edition is Part 1 of a two-part newsletter covering the best faceless content formats.

Faceless TikTok/IG is, for some, an entry point into TikTok marketing, for others, the best way to create content for their niche, and for many, a strategy to scale aggressively.

There are countless ways to approach it, and founders and marketers have found success in nearly every vertical.

Let’s break down a few of them, with examples, to see what they do well—and exactly how they do it.

Slideshows

Flamingo, a question game app for couples, is ranking #34 with $70K MRR and has multiple accounts using slideshow content racking up millions of views.

They perform well on TikTok and even better on Instagram. Relationship-related content thrives on Instagram because partners can easily share it with each other (whereas TikTok might be more of a single player or more of an “internet-friend” platform).

Their posts are highly saveable, allowing users to reference the questions later or take the next step through the CTA at the end.

This type of content drives high volume but low conversions. That’s why, to make this strategy work, you typically need to run 8 to 20+ accounts.

However, the necessary volume is largely offset by how cost-effective it is to operate these accounts (yes, it’s almost cost-less. Minus the posting).

How to Create Them

There are two main ways to do this.

First, start with Figma. Design a simple background and add lines of frames where you’ll place the questions.

The key is ensuring the questions make sense together (to max viewer’s retention).

The hooks here are incredibly effective:

“7 questions to ask your mum before it’s too late.”

“5 questions to ask him tonight.”

Both tap into personal connection (“your mum” and “him”) and create urgency (“before it’s too late” and “tonight”).

Because this format is infinitely reproducible, it can become a sustainable long-term strategy.

On Instagram, you’ll need to turn these into videos. Either as auto-scrolling slideshows or with a simple animated background (like moving clouds) while the text updates on top.

Clipping

Pray.com and DeathClock are two examples of apps thriving by repurposing clipped content from all over the internet—mainly from podcasts and shows.

I’m a huge fan of clipping, and I think every app should have a clipping channel within its niche.

It’s a simple yet powerful way to niche down a channel and provide valuable content tailored to the right audience. Esp as it features a recognizable figure they already know, trust, or even admire.

Praydotcom uses well-known figures, clipping parts of podcasts and shows where they talk about faith and God. They edit the clips in black and white with a dramatic effect to enhance engagement.

DeathClock takes a dual approach: clipping both podcast guests and himself.

Even better, he’s not actually hosting a podcast.

He’s just at home with a podcast setup, monologuing about what he knows, creating the illusion of the format.

How to Create Them

The agency behind DeathClock’s content reached out to me, and here’s how they’re set up:

They have one person in the U.S. handling timestamps.

She’s finding the right story and angle, while multiple editors in the Philippines handle the editing for cost efficiency.

This setup allows them to produce content in bulk. And at scale.

For regular podcast clips, the process is a bit trickier. You need a reliable way to source content.

The best approach is to follow the model of TV news channels, which maintain a database of pre-labeled content, making it easy to find relevant clips quickly.

Alternatively, you can manually scour the internet to find the right clips, though this is far more time-consuming.

Brain Rot

Brainrot is a style that became popular through two-faced videos. It typically takes one of two forms:

A Minecraft parkour background with a story (often an iMessage conversation) overlaid—like what Rizz App made famous.

A split-screen format, with a “satisfying” video running on one side (bottom or left) and a clip or podcast on the other (top or right).

This format isn’t just engaging—it’s also a hack to bypass TikTok’s duplicate content detection. By constantly changing the background, your content avoids being flagged as a duplicate.

Rizz App popularized this style in the consumer app space.

Like most faceless content strategies, it’s high volume, low conversion. But with hundreds of millions of views and a well-targeted vertical, even low conversion rates can bring in tens, if not hundreds of thousands of users.

How to Create Them

You can create these manually by downloading hours-long Minecraft parkour videos (on YouTube) and cutting them in CapCut, or by using automation tools like Crayo (not a user).

The most important element is the story you layer on top. It needs to be carefully written and tailored to your vertical.

This style won’t work in every niche.

I’d recommend using AI only to create variations, not to write the stories themselves.

To get real engagement, you need to deeply understand your audience and craft your narratives with precision.

Screen Recs

Straight screen recordings from your app can be highly effective. But only if your app is a creative or messaging app.

This format works exceptionally well for apps that introduce a new way to communicate, especially those targeting Gen Z.

One key detail you’ll notice here is the background.

They’re using a brainrot-style approach, layering an ultra-slow-moving HD video of an office or home space behind the screen recording.

This two-layer effect enhances the user experience and makes the content more engaging.

In this case, they benefit from both the storytelling power of a text-based app (similar to Rizz) and the creativity of their freeform chat feature, making the videos far more compelling.

This format is infinitely repeatable. The challenge is finding enough accounts and posters to distribute the content at scale.

How to Create Them

The backgrounds are either custom-made in their offices or sourced from HD videos, with a subtle twist or glitch effect added for style.

The screen-recorded stories are done manually between two team members. (If not for the creative aspect, this could technically be automated.)

The process:

Write the stories

Record the interactions

Edit in CapCut or DaVinci

Post with a trending sound + caption

Done.

—

That wraps up Part 1 of this faceless edition. In the next edition, I’ll cover 5 more faceless formats crushing on TikTok/Reels.

Stay tuned.

And if you’re not subscribed yet, Maria (genius growth hacker in the team) runs another bite-sized newsletter, sharing viral trends and formats she finds on TikTok every other day. You can check it out here: https://tiktoktrends.beehiiv.com/subscribe

Until next time,

The Social Growth Engineers Team

frameworks.name: Faceless Content Formats
frameworks.description: A set of content creation strategies that do not require showing faces, leveraging formats like slideshows, clipping, brain rot, and screen recordings to drive viral growth and engagement on TikTok and Instagram.
frameworks.when_to_use: When aiming to scale content production rapidly and cost-effectively on TikTok and Instagram, especially for consumer apps targeting Gen Z or niche communities where personal connection or storytelling is key.
frameworks.example: Flamingo app uses slideshow question formats to engage couples on Instagram, while Pray.com clips faith-related podcast content to build trust and niche authority.

frameworks.name: High-Volume Multi-Account Strategy
frameworks.description: Operating multiple accounts (8-20+) posting faceless content to generate high volume views and compensate for low conversion rates per account, leveraging cost-effective content production.
frameworks.when_to_use: When individual content pieces have low conversion but high engagement potential, and the cost of content creation is low enough to scale across many accounts.
frameworks.example: Flamingo runs multiple slideshow accounts to accumulate millions of views and drive installs despite low conversion per post.

frameworks.name: Content Clipping and Repurposing
frameworks.description: Sourcing and editing short clips from podcasts, shows, or other media featuring trusted figures to create niche-relevant, engaging content that builds authority and trust.
frameworks.when_to_use: When your app or brand aligns with a niche that has existing trusted content creators or influencers, and you want to leverage their authority without producing all original content.
frameworks.example: Pray.com clips faith-related podcast segments with dramatic black-and-white edits to engage their audience.

frameworks.name: Brain Rot Format
frameworks.description: Using split-screen or two-faced video formats with engaging backgrounds and overlaid stories or conversations to increase engagement and bypass duplicate content detection on TikTok.
frameworks.when_to_use: When you want to create highly engaging, repeatable content that can be varied easily to avoid platform penalties and appeal to younger audiences.
frameworks.example: Rizz App uses Minecraft parkour backgrounds with iMessage-style stories to drive hundreds of millions of views.

frameworks.name: Screen Recording with Creative Backgrounds
frameworks.description: Recording app interactions layered over subtle, slow-moving HD backgrounds to showcase app features in a visually appealing way, especially for creative or messaging apps.
frameworks.when_to_use: When your app offers unique communication or creative features that can be demonstrated visually, targeting Gen Z or creative users.
frameworks.example: Apps use screen recordings with brainrot-style backgrounds and trending sounds to create compelling TikTok videos.

metadata.key_principle: Faceless content formats enable scalable, cost-effective, and viral content creation by leveraging storytelling, niche relevance, and platform-specific engagement hacks without relying on personal branding or influencer presence.
metadata.article_summary: The article explores multiple faceless TikTok and Instagram content formats—slideshows, clipping, brain rot, and screen recordings—that consumer apps use to drive viral growth and engagement. Each format is explained with examples and practical creation tips. The strategies emphasize high-volume, low-cost content production, leveraging personal connection, trusted figures, and creative storytelling to engage niche audiences. These formats help apps scale organic growth and user acquisition effectively on social platforms.

frameworks.name: UGC Network Strategy
frameworks.description: Build a network of multiple user-generated content accounts, each targeting different angles or features of the app, to maximize reach and virality on platforms like TikTok.
frameworks.when_to_use: When launching or scaling a consumer app that benefits from authentic peer content and viral social proof, especially on TikTok or Instagram.
frameworks.example: Musa created 18 TikTok accounts with different creators, each producing content around the app's features, resulting in over 10M views and 30K monthly downloads within one month.

frameworks.name: Hook-Driven Creator Content
frameworks.description: Use strong emotional or relatable hooks in short videos, such as personal testimonials or surprising statements, to capture attention quickly and encourage engagement.
frameworks.when_to_use: For apps targeting younger demographics on TikTok or Instagram where quick engagement is critical to virality.
frameworks.example: A creator's video with the hook '10 years of using a male designed period app and now I find this…' went viral with over 1.2M views.

frameworks.name: Feature-Focused Content Channels
frameworks.description: Create dedicated content channels or accounts that focus on specific app features or unique content styles to deepen engagement and attract niche audiences.
frameworks.when_to_use: When the app has multiple unique features that can each appeal to different user segments or content trends.
frameworks.example: Musa's 'hormonscope' TikTok account focused on daily cycle predictions, blending app features with zodiac content to attract a niche audience.

metadata.key_principle: Leveraging a diversified network of authentic user-generated content accounts with strong hooks and feature-focused themes drives rapid organic growth and virality on TikTok.
metadata.article_summary: Musa, a gamified period tracking app, achieved over 10 million TikTok views and 30,000 monthly downloads within one month by deploying a network of 18 UGC TikTok accounts. Each account used strong emotional hooks and focused on different app features, such as a virtual pet mascot and cycle-based daily predictions. This diversified UGC strategy enabled rapid viral growth and community building despite some user concerns about data privacy.

companies_mentioned.name: Musa
companies_mentioned.lesson: Building a network of UGC creators with strong hooks and feature-focused content can drive rapid TikTok virality and downloads.

content_patterns.name: Hook-Driven Personal Testimonial
content_patterns.description: Creators share personal stories or surprising insights to hook viewers quickly.
content_patterns.example: A creator expressing shock about switching from male-designed period apps to Musa.

content_patterns.name: Feature Highlight with Visuals
content_patterns.description: Creators talk to the camera while showing in-app screenshots or mascots to demonstrate app features.
content_patterns.example: Videos showing the purple dragon mascot and daily tasks in the app.

content_patterns.name: Faceless Content with Trend Integration
content_patterns.description: Using faceless videos combined with trending themes like zodiac signs to appeal to niche audiences.
content_patterns.example: The 'hormonscope' account blending cycle predictions with zodiac content.

Art Workout is generating almost 1/2m downloads every month and over $200K MRR.

App was released in 2021 to teach how to draw (lessons, challenges, etc).

They’re running a HUGE network on TikTok:

I found 23 accounts totaling 239,128,300 views

95% faceless content!!

Strategy part 1/2 ????????

Multiple accounts per language

Spanish: tt@artworkout_es and tt@artworkout_lat

French: tt@artworkout.fr

English: several, main one is tt@artworkout_app

Arabic: tt@artworkout_ar

Portuguese: tt@artworkoutbr

All videos are

100% faceless, either in-app recording or iPad recorded w/ hand drawing

tt@artworkout_es is the most viral account (61.7M views)

Most viral videos show this app feature where you can draw at the same time as a stranger:

This video posted 4d ago got:

Strategy part 2/2 ????????

The main accounts are on

frameworks.name: Multi-Account Multi-Language Network
frameworks.description: Create multiple TikTok accounts targeting different languages and regions to maximize reach and virality in diverse markets. Each account posts faceless content tailored to the language and culture, increasing relevance and engagement.
frameworks.when_to_use: When aiming to scale user acquisition and brand awareness globally across different language-speaking audiences.
frameworks.example: ArtWorkout runs 20+ TikTok accounts in languages like Spanish, French, Arabic, Portuguese, and English, collectively generating over 239 million views.

frameworks.name: Faceless UGC Content Strategy
frameworks.description: Leverage user-generated content that is faceless (no personal identity shown) to create scalable, relatable, and viral videos that focus on the product experience rather than personalities. This reduces creator dependency and increases content volume.
frameworks.when_to_use: When wanting to scale content creation rapidly without relying on influencer personalities, and to appeal broadly without cultural or personal bias.
frameworks.example: ArtWorkout’s TikTok accounts post 95% faceless videos showing app features like drawing with strangers, driving millions of views and engagement.

frameworks.name: Viral Audio Trend Leveraging
frameworks.description: Consistently update and test videos with trending TikTok audio clips to increase discoverability and virality. Using popular sounds helps videos appear in more feeds and taps into existing viral momentum.
frameworks.when_to_use: When producing repetitive or similar content formats and needing to boost organic reach and engagement on TikTok or similar platforms.
frameworks.example: ArtWorkout frequently changes the audio in their videos to the latest viral sounds, helping their faceless content go viral repeatedly.

metadata.key_principle: Scaling growth on TikTok can be achieved by combining multi-language faceless content accounts with UGC strategies and leveraging trending audio to maximize organic reach and downloads.
metadata.article_summary: ArtWorkout scaled to over 500K monthly downloads and $200K MRR by running 20+ TikTok accounts across multiple languages, posting mostly faceless UGC videos showcasing app features. They leverage viral audio trends to boost discoverability and have expanded to Instagram and YouTube with less success. Their strategy focuses on broad organic growth through content volume, language targeting, and trend adaptation.

companies_mentioned.name: ArtWorkout
companies_mentioned.lesson: Using a multi-account, multi-language TikTok strategy with faceless UGC content and viral audio trends can drive massive organic downloads and revenue.

content_patterns.name: Faceless UGC Videos

content_patterns.example: ArtWorkout’s drawing-with-strangers videos recorded on iPad without showing faces.

content_patterns.name: Multi-Language Accounts
content_patterns.description: Separate TikTok accounts targeting different languages to localize content and increase relevance in diverse markets.
content_patterns.example: ArtWorkout’s Spanish, French, Arabic, Portuguese, and English TikTok accounts.

content_patterns.name: Trend Audio Swapping
content_patterns.description: Regularly updating videos with trending audio clips to ride viral waves and increase organic reach.
content_patterns.example: ArtWorkout changing audio on similar videos to the latest TikTok viral sounds.

Content is often faceless and bulk produced

$1,000,000 MRR (app only) and 202 Million views on TikTok & Reels

How the hobby of ⅓ of Americans turned into a money making machine:

Bird Buddy is a bird watching company selling cameras, accessories & bird houses. In 2022, they released an app that pairs with the camera to monitor bird visits and that can also be used alone to see what others are sharing with the community.

The app alone is generating $1,000,000 MRR:

In total they’ve made over $105,000,000 and sold 350,000 feeders

They’re running accounts on every social media platform – TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, Reddit, X:

One account per channel, but check this:

More than 202,000,000 views on 2 accounts (TikTok & Reels)

Why they’re doing everything right:

1/ riding trends

This video is using a viral audio (from a while ago)

Ups discovery and makes people watch (even those who don’t care about birds)

On a similar note,

2/ ride viral events

After Duolingo announced Duo’s death, they posted this:

3/ all content is proof of product

Most of their content follows the same format

POV from bird house camera + closeup of birds who stop there

=> when you watch a video, you get a direct sense of product value (no other CTA needed)

Either video (like above) or slideshow

Like this one => 9.1M views, 1.6M likes, 6.7K comments, 156K bookmarks

Hook “ You better not mess with my gang, or you’ll be messing with…”

Their trick is just

4/ great storytelling

They could be posting videos of birds and mention their breeds, etc

No one would care, so instead they created stories and characters around their content:

Ex: there’s this bird they call Larry

There’s even users commenting on other videos asking for more Larry content

From last week, over 500 comments and 68K likes

Insight – if your niche is too small and/or plain boring:

Spin your content to match your niche in format/visuals but add layers of interest and relatability with characters, storylines between them, cross over with other apps/events, self-id hack (ex: “which bird are you based on your sign”) etc

On Instagram they’re doing the same:

94.9M views in total, same content

On YouTube they’re doing Shorts (same content) and long form

Different series => cool bird facts, tutorials for camera setup, product launches, etc

And the coolest part:

Reddit community with 3.9K members

People share their bird footage from their cameras & even compete for “best bird award” and stuff like that:

Building a community is possible for any niche but especially powerful if your app taps into a hobby/passion => word of mouth

Don’t sleep on it

98% of consumer app founders never think of this UGC scaling hack.

It’s SO simple yet can make you save 000s of dollars:

Sitly is a Dutch app launched 2 years ago.

They’re generating $250,000 MRR (80K downloads last month)

6 accounts doing 106,813,700 views in total:

Each of these accounts are targeting a different country

They mix formats but best performing videos are UGC formatted

But here’s the catch:

They use the exact same creator & exact same video for all languages

All they do is translate the text hook.

This same video got:

9.9M views & 49K likes => Netherlands

8.2M views & 63K likes => Germany

1.3M views & 10K likes => Spain

525K views & 8K likes => Canada

Formula:

1/ Select your top performing UGC creator

2/ Have them record 5-10 videos (faceful, non-talking OR lip-syncing to viral audio)

3/ Write hook, translate in all languages & post

4/ Make sure you make any small adjustments, like

Sitly’s hook mentions babysitting pay per hour

So they change it to reflect each country (NL – 15€, ES – 12€, IT – 10€)

You can use this to create dozens of language-specific UGC accounts at a fraction of cost

Relying on only your top 2-3 UGC creators

frameworks.when_to_use: When you have proven UGC content that performs well in one market and want to scale efficiently into multiple language markets without creating entirely new content for each.
frameworks.example: Sitly used one creator's video and translated the hook into 4 languages, adjusting babysitting pay rates per country, resulting in over 100M views across different countries.

Widgify briefly took the #1 spot on the App Store.

Widgify, Mico, iScreens <> Locket, Yope, CoupleJoy

The cute lock screen widget war is raging.

Everyone is after the most retentive real estate on your phone ????

I’m seeing many more TikTok strategies from cute widget apps those days.

I wrote about Locket, Yope and Couplejoy here:

https://x.com/iamgdsa/status/1820745660284416122

https://x.com/iamgdsa/status/1889326927531372626

Mico, Widgify competitor, also ranks high (#5).

Both Widgify and Micro are using similar strategies with high aesthetic creators.

There is a massive niche of Korean/Japanese/Asian aesthetic videos like:

Widgify and Mico main accounts are respectively generating 3M and 38M views running faceless high aesthetic content.

Mico seems to have at least one other dedicated Mico Widget account tt@phone.beautifier.

The account started as something else. They probably bought the creator with a retainer after a first collab.

Some posts probably have been ad boosted on this one.

Proving that the content format works, Licowa tt@licowa.app, a similar app started recently (few weeks) already doing decent with a similar strategy on a new account.

Widgify isn’t running more dedicated accounts (or i couldn’t find them) but doing an increasing amount of influencer partnerships.

Many many videos from micro, and even larger creators are promoting the widget app in this niche.

Another interesting niche to leverage is the “Phone Refresh” trend.

This account is likely running a two-in-one business. First one is a regular phone refurbishment service, which fuels the second biz: generating millions of views on TikTok.

Note that tt@jessica.ranngel in this video has a Widgify link in her bio.

Imo, every phone or device repair shop should consider starting an account like this.

Another interesting faceless content strategy is accounts like this tt@mo0nlunar.

Every edit is similar and the concept is highly scalable (in terms of production costs etc…)

Account is just pushing different apps every video (with Mico being the most prominent).

You can run this type of account as a company, and/or create them as an individual and net the collabs.

tt@bibiesant

tt@tamirisrlopes1

tt@kithlanga

Are more examples of aesthetic iphone ugc accounts. Promoting various things + d2c affiliates.

These are potential scaling strategies for couple widget apps like Locket, Yope, CoupleJoy, etc.

I think other social apps with incredible levels of design, like Amo/Bump, could absolutely crush it by creating content in this TT niche.

There have to be ways to automate and scale these faceless aesthetic videos.

One person working full-time could produce maybe 40 to 50 videos a day. With an offshore PH editor, costs could stay low.

From there, you can launch multiple accounts and scale, the same way aesthetic study-related TikTok accounts are doing.

Linda Shad’s growth hacking to a $17K+ MRR indie business:

Linda Shad started posting videos of her drawings on TikTok in 2016

After her 1st video went viral (500K views), 100 people signed up for her Discord group

A bit after she met Ben and they started working together

& found a name and concept for the project

Meanwhile, another video exploded (10M views), and 150,000 people joined Discord

So they launched the first version of Voidpet:

At the time as a self-care game, then they developed it to become a gamified journaling app

Voidpet: Mental Health => 10K+ monthly downloads & $9K MRR

Users collect and evolve emotion-based creatures & track their mood/habits

And one year later, she launched a new one: Voidpet Dungeon

Launched 3 months ago => 7K monthly downloads & $8K MRR

It’s the same characters but in a more gamified way (kinda like Pokemon)

On her TikTok account (tt@lindashad) she has 214K followers

SGE Team

February 11, 2025

4 min read

Save for later

Yope social app did 120M+ views in 3 months.

5.3M shares, 1.5M bookmarks. Now scaling to a 45+ creator network accounts.

I can’t believe I am just finding this alpha now…

Full TikTok organic strategy exposed ????

It’s like Locket, but for a friend group.

A subtle variation, but the key difference is that they focus on videos for the Spanish-language market.

Out of 40 accounts, more than 50% are in Spanish.

Each account posts twice a day, with over 1,500 videos posted to date.

The Spanish accounts are performing incredibly well, with tt@mar_yope leading the way—averaging 110K views, with the highest reaching 5.3M.

Check out this English account: tt@janin.yope.

It took her 70 videos before hitting her first viral one at 1M views.

Now, she has videos with 4.4M, 5.3M, and 2.5M views on top of that first one.

Good things take time. Building strong accounts and fine-tuning them is key.

The idea that “post every day and you’ll be rewarded” by the TikTok algorithm can definitely be real.

It took 45 videos for tt@yrrah.yope to get a breakthrough.

Now, she has 6 videos over 1M views and 35 videos performing 10x better than the median.

Formats vary from text posts, with hooks like:

“Me explaining to my boyfriend how we literally have 4 DAYS to download Yope so that on January 1st we can create a secret album of us, and at the end of the year have a recap movie with all our memories.”

to Locket app-style videos with hook to app demo:

From talking videos to slideshows to memes. they’re exceptionally good at building accounts.

I’ve gathered all their hooks, translated them into English, and analyzed the stats.

You’ll get everything—hooks, stats, and insights across multiple data dimensions. (yes, free, as usual)

Download the dataset here:

https://www.socialgrowthengineers.com/resources/yope

Also, check out this public Shortimize collection I made with their accounts:

https://app.shortimize.com/c/2a10LRktXegbb2

It looks like they’re a Ukrainian company now operating from London.

That could explain why they’re targeting EU markets—or it might just be a strategic move.

I found one Polish account, and they might have more niche EU ones.

They started by targeting multiple languages and successfully built viral accounts in each one.

Now, they’re scaling up, with 15 new accounts launched in the past two weeks.

The app was created in 2022, but they only started this multi-account UGC strategy three months ago.

And now, they’re absolutely crushing it.

There are three ways to do a solo or bootstrapped founder IG/TikTok viral account:

Informational

Demo

Founder-story

Informational

My favorite one. It’s about generating educational / informational content within your niche.

Founders sleep on this one a lot. It’s the strategy that ripples long-term while also being effective short-term.

A great example is the Oasis Water app (38M views):

By growing such an account, you essentially create a “media” page within your vertical.

Using your own product as a background asset in the video content, you naturally create an authentic acquisition machine.

The solution is nested with the problem.

Oasis’ founder averages 30K views per video and has multiple viral hits. He’s making tens of thousands of $ a month from this. Solo.

In most cases, you’re building a product you already have expertise in so it’s rather effortless to turn your domain knowledge into your own little media machine.

Demo

The faceless demo format is a great way to get into short form video content.

If you have a “disruptive” (or just different enough) app, film your phone giving a tutorial or showcasing the app/website with catchy hooks and story lines.

Repeat this daily with slight tweaks, study retention rates to improve hooks and edits. Eventually, you will crack the code for viral demo videos.

Dump Phone shows how it’s done:

His best videos did 10K+ bookmarks, and netted him thousands of downloads.

It’s accessible and it’s faceless. Give it a try.

Founder-story

The last one, is the explanatory format.

“I built an app…” format works on both IG and TikTok.

The founder of this fit-check app nailed it, repeatedly:

Use long text overlays to tell why you built the product: like “X and Y had a baby.” or story tell why and how you’re building the app.

It’s optimal for social or Gen Z-focused apps (also works for other types of apps).

In the case above, he’s doing 7-second videos with a long story text over himself frantically moving around.

One “talking head” variation by Josh Rozin, where he pitches his new app, following the same “X and Y had a baby” narrative than above:

One more edited variation by Miquel, where he built an account showcasing his team building the app live. With this strategy, he got 1M+ downloads and #1 in Spain:

Post daily, or multiple times a day, tweak, and let the algorithm do its thing.

Coconote AI (9mo-old):

> $200K MRR & 40K/mo downloads

> 259,421,033 total views

The UGC/AI Study playbook these apps keep copy & pasting (and winning):

Coconote AI (love the name) was released in April last year

It’s AI note-taking meets gaming b-roll footage, aka “Pdf to brain rot” concept which they turned into a landing page:

With CTA to download the app the website is getting 19.5K daily organic visitors.

They’re running content on TikTok, IG Reels and (a bit) on Youtube Shorts:

In just 7 accounts, they reached 259,421,033 views.  5 out of the 7 are UGC accounts, fully dedicated and run by student creators.

Last Nov 18th, their views peaked with one single TikTok video (tt@sidstudiesadhd):

That went insanely viral => 41M views, 4.5M likes, 10.7K comments & 535.7K bookmarks.

How? They rode the #womeninmalefields trend at the right time and in the right way.

Hook: “Oh he don’t wanna read all that?” + recording laptop screen

And check how they included the CTA:

Caption: “this trend is killlliing me lmao (website is Coconote ai for those of you asking)”

It’s “UGC-like”, but direct enough to convert views into downloads (+ using a  trending hashtag).

On ig@coconote.app, they repeat formats straight out of the AI’s study tool playbook (LITERALLY):

1. Hot teacher hook

They use a super attractive guy as “professor” to spark views

They have 30+ videos with this exact same footage, some went viral (like this one) => 4M views, 18K likes, 500 comments

But THIS is the crazy part:

This guy is the exact same guy on Turbolearn’s posts.

Remember them?

Clearly they’re all repurposing the same videos from each other (or maybe they “took” them from some other account at first):

Similar to how they’re doing their second format:

2. Lecture hall recording

Over the shoulder and in-class recordings

Familiar again? That’s because it’s the exact same playbook used by Answer AI (and Chart AI, Quizard AI, etc etc)

Don’t fret over being original, because you’ll probably be copied anyways (or would be better off copying off of someone else’s good strategy.)

Sometimes even using the exact same video and your own app edit.

Focus on great hooks, effective CTAs and keeping engagement high.

Simplify everything else down to the minimum effort.

Save for later

This app got: 537M views, 58M likes, 114K comments & 2M saves-in less than 60 videos posted across TikTok and Reels.  Now they’re turning a viral format into an app.

Starting with distribution:

Both accounts were created at the end of 2023 (tt@lifeonfilm.27 & ig@lifeonfilm.27)

Concept is insanely easy & cool: This guy distributes a disposable camera to different strangers/groups before they go traveling/partying, then they return them and he makes a video with all the analog pictures

I’ve never seen such virality time and time again in the same account

Videos are all similar to this:

All with the same text hook: “Giving disposable cameras to strangers”

And it’s not just views, engagement is also crazy:

This video => 28M views, 4.9M likes, 5.8K comments, 319K bookmarks

He’s posting the same content on both TikTok & Reels

Interestingly, the most viral videos are not the same across both platforms (even though the format is the exact same)

This is the most viral on Reels => 42M views, 3.8M likes, 6.5K comments.

3 months ago, he created an app – Life on film (video/photo editor to produce a similar vibe)

Still at 10K/mo downloads

He uses comments where people ask for the type of camera to direct them to the link in bio (download the app)

In my opinion, it’s lacking a connection between the concept and videos that millions of people love, and the app itself

As soon as he integrates a more direct CTA or diversifies strategy to (also) UGC, I see downloads spiking really fast.

2 brothers launched a stop-scroll app in 2022

Currently at $20K MRR over 40K/mo downloads

Takes less than 2h/week to replicate their most viral TikTok format (40M views):

BePresent is a productivity & screen-time app founded by brothers Jack & Charles Winston

They are running 7 TikTok accounts & 2 on IG Reels.

Up until last summer,

They had only one account tt@screentimejesus

That’s Jack’s founder account with 4,409,000 total views

Not much, but all viral videos followed this same format:

Jack recording himself talking, holding phone/camera while recording

And title hook overlay “Signs you need a dopamine detox” // “How I reduced my screen time from 7h+ to 1h”, etc

3 videos above 1M views (each)

In April last year, they replicated same strategy:

And created Charles’ founder account

Only 144,000 views total & just one viral video

Almost all videos are a recording of his face outside + white text overlay

Interestingly, they insisted on this format on 2 other accounts:

tt@bepresentbros => 3rd founder account for both brothers

By far their best performing acc => 40,400,000 total views

They alternate between two similar (viral) formats:

Same video style as above (face recordings mostly outside + long text hook overlay)

They drink/eat/smile/walk but never talk to the camera & they always add a trending audio

=> 7.7M views // 112K likes // 825 comments // 6K bookmarks

Slideshows

Cover photo with creator selfie + long white text overlay (similar to videos above)

After 1st slide, the rest are all in-app screenshots/phone pictures w/ text desc

=> 8.9M views // 215K likes // 419 comments // 50K bookmarks

Clever detail here:

They recycle the same cover photo more than once

Desk photo used 4x, car selfie used 6x, walking used 2x

This last one has two videos: one got 0 views, another did 2.9M

Crazy easy to bulk produce

You can take 5 selfies in 10 mins, write 7 hook variations in 30mins and you have content for a whole week

This blonde girl creator now has her own BePresent account (tt@el.bepresent)

Started posting one month ago, 1x day

Still not performing (44K views), but posting the exact same content type

Curious to see if they’ll expand their UGC creator network like so many others are doing

I’ve noticed an interesting psychology pattern among many consumer app viral videos

Like this one => 50.2M views, 534K likes, 3K comments and 144K bookmarks

The “too good to be true”/instant reward hack:

“If you have anxiety, listen to this sound and watch what it does to your brain”

You can add a time/effort frame: “If you have anxiety, listen to this for 55 seconds and see…” (careful though, 55 sec in 2025 it’s not so little and could backfire)

Or you can even do what they did here and add a question : “what’s your favorite?” to spark engagement

This video got 1.7M views & 6K comments (vs the previous one which had 5M views but only 1K comments)

All these examples are from Calm App (tt@calm), one of the oldest and largest meditation apps ($60M+ ARR)

They’re doing insanely well organically with this 100% faceless format

But what’s cool is that you can offer “instant reward” for any niche:

Check this example from a language learning app:

“How to be fluent in Korean with

ONE

word”

=> 1.9M views // 353K likes // 1.7K comments // 53K bookmarks:

It should feel just “impossible” enough that triggers attention

The bigger the promise & the shorter the catch (time, effort, etc) the better => it’s the “too good to be true effect”

And another example:

Viral format #1 – Educational parking videos with AI animation

11M views // 562K likes // 1627 comments // 238K saves

pic.twitter.com/RCBYtYebEK

— Maria Inês (@themariaines)

December 28, 2024

“How to parallel park your car in 5 steps”

Seems obvious but it works, but only if your app/content targets a real pain point

In all these cases:

Feeling anxious affects daily life of millions

Learning Korean is challenging

Learning how to parallel park is even harder (for some of us, we listen and we don’t judge)

If it sounds too good to be true but still somewhat believable, you’ll have their attention

frameworks.example: "If you have anxiety, listen to this sound for 30 seconds and watch what it does to your brain" or "How to be fluent in Korean with ONE word".

These hooks trigger curiosity and engagement by addressing real pain points with bold but believable claims, often paired with a short time or effort frame. This format works well on TikTok and Instagram, driving organic growth and user acquisition through viral videos and faceless content.

Long-distance relationship apps are optimized for short-form video marketing.

CoupleJoy’s $75K MRR and 80K monthly downloads prove it.

They ran Locket’s creator playbook to hit 9.5M views in just 25 days:

Couple Joy targets long-distance couples offering widgets, shared timelines, games, questions, blabla…

Their main account (tt@couplejoy) doesn’t have much viral/frequent posts.

They built a creator multi-account strategy 25 days ago with at least:

8 fully dedicated accounts running and posting everyday (6 creators and 2 faceless).

7.3M views, 60K bookmarks & an astonishing 10%+ hit rate.

Check here:

https://app.shortimize.com/c/2a10SxOScOuiUG

3 of these accounts are faceless (incl. main one)

One of these accounts produces content in French only. One in Spanish only.

Interesting language approach that also isolates them from the US ban.

The app has been running for 2 years, so they probably already had a substantial user base and knew which countries to target.

They have 2 performing faceless formats:

Screen recording of app (or widget on home screen)

& text hook “I just found an app for my long distance relationship”, “I can’t believe I found this lockscreen widget”…

This one did 358K views, 13K likes, 114 comments, 2.3K bookmarks.

Game/questions slideshow

2 of the accounts are getting good views/engagement with this.

tt@pour_couples does this interesting format with complete black screen, white text and one emoji on the cover:

But the most viral videos are from their 6 creator accounts.

They usually incl. female creator “shocked”/”emotional” face + screen recordings of the app

Like this one which did 1.3M views, 67K likes & 22K bookmarks.

This one in Spanish, also having astonishing performances (tt@marcouplejoy):

I found another app being promoted by one of the same creators.

Different account, different dev companies & different app. But doing the exact same product/TikTok strategy.

Outside was also released in 2022, as a Social calendar with countdown features to share events w/ friends, family, etc

Running same strategy – same creators:

https://app.shortimize.com/c/2a10TqpgpELkwM

They have way less downloads (~10K/mo) but in an interesting format got 2 videos over 1.8m.

Normal couple hugging/ airport footage & hook, but B&W effect:

Astrology apps are 100% a distribution play.

This one below hit $90K MRR & 80K downloads experimenting with 5 different short form video formats.

It’s a gold mine for organic TikTok/IG.

Having explored the market broadly, most of those apps are similar.

Past a good product (like Co-Star or The Pattern), AstroClub also figured that it’s about distribution.

They have 5 branded accounts:

Memes & slideshows: tt@astroclub_fan

Most recent channel started in November. They’ve reached 1.6M views with 38 slideshows. They’re posting once a every few days with the same format:

Re-purposed images in 4×4 grid with a quote in the middle. Centered around stars at first:

And then moved to more lifestyle general public slideshows:

Straightforward to make with re-purposed content (can outsource the designs past discovery) and generate a ton of engagement & shares (%cr to downloads? questionable, prob low)

Street interviews: tt@astroclub_app

Well edited videos performing well. Can be recorded in quantity and are mixed & remixed. Some did millions of views and shares/engagement. They’ve mixed this format with more vlog/explanatory videos (not sure why)

UGC + hook overlay tt@astroclub.app

They used to have this one ugc creator consistently posting on this account.

They’ve moved to having different ugc content mixed with some AI content (not sure how performant this is now)

Daily horoscopes tt@horoscope.astroclub

Most recent account where they push daily horoscopes.

It’s not yet performing but they keep posting daily.

tt@astroclub.zodiacs has other horoscopes & zodiac readings. This performs better than the previous one, with almost a million views and bookmarks.

Content around astrology is wild.

I found three more formats they could explore:

tt@astrolobby & tt@astrologiequotidien

Full AI account in French running for a while about Astrology. Slow transitions. Well executed editing from AI transitions.

tt@zodiac.powerrr doing interesting AI / brainrot repetitive slideshow storytelling.

Account isn’t promoting much but trying to monetize through collabs. Median view count is insane (some app should just buy this account)

tt@zodiax_fax_ is doing zodiac memes. Another high performing format. Those are very sharable. Most are re-purposed content with zodiac signs overlayed on top:

#1 in Lifestyle, 7K new users per HOUR and already generating 6-figures in MRR

Some of the team behind the viral app Pengu launched this new side project just 10 days ago.

App is a “Spotify Wrapped” for Whatsapp. Export chat > run through LLM and get > Total messages sent, % people ghosted, screenshots taken, etc.

They hide half the wrap then $4.99/wk. UX is dead simple.

Started aggressively pushing on TikTok in 3 ways:

On Pengu’s page (tt@playpengu). They used the account’s existing juice to do: 12 videos in 5 days and made 961,786 views & good engagement.

That’s solid, but this is how they broke the game:

New dedicated “UGC” accounts. Found 3 new ones and 2 bit older ones that were used to promote Pengu and now switched.

One of these videos went viral (tt@lotti2059). I put the screenshot and not the video as she speaks German.

2.1M views, 113K likes, 921 comments & 11.4K bookmarks:

All videos go under the hashtag

#whatswhatsappwrapped

Including now some organic content made by some larger TikTok creators:

Like this one (tt@beroslife), who likely picked up the app from somewhere and made a video (they said they spent $0 so I assume it’s organically spreading in germany now).

1.1M views, 28K likes, 1.3K comments & 6K bookmarks (20h after posting)

Now they could activate their other Pengu TikTok accounts to turn even more views into even more $$$.

That’s just in Germany. They’ll probably replicate in other countries.

If not, I already told my friend in France who’s making a French clone. I assume there will be 10+ country focused versions in the next few days.

Toca Boca has 100s of users generating daily content for them on TikTok. Bringing in 1.5B+ views and 10M+ bookmarks.

They didn’t spend a dime.

A thread for “gaming or creative” apps that want to put their acquisition on autopilot and win long term:

Toca Boca is a sandbox/creative game. It’s currently #8 in Education.

Went up to #2 during Christmas:

I’ve collected 50 accounts (there are more). Those are users, mostly teens, posting daily creative content from the game. So that you get the scale, over the past two years, those accounts generated

1.6Bn views and 10M bookmarks.

The content they post looks like this. Community is gigantic & they interact with each others’ posts generating heavy (natural) engagement.

They come from various countries.

From a sample of 10 accounts, i found: 2x RU, KZ, DK, 3x US, BR, AT, TR

Look at those accounts, they’re clearly trying to grow and farm attention.

So the question is, how do you create such fans and/or a community that’ll want or be intrinsically incentivized to build up an account and create daily content without asking nothing in return?

Those kids are self-rewarding themselves through the dopamine it gives them getting views and building (street) cred.

It makes total sense and looks exactly like what happened for Incredibox.

This is clearly a mid/late stage growth strategy here, once a core daily active user base has been nurtured: let them build their own communities and sub cultures.

They probably made Discord servers and Subreddits too.

But can you take the lead and create/promote those communities yourself Get control over pushing the incentives and be able to bootstrap such TikTok/IG ugc networks.

One could showcase the dopamine/cred gained of having such accounts by engineering the first few for instance. Build them up in-house or through paying a handful of core users to do so, and then somehow let them be discovered by the rest of the community.

Proving you can still beat an over-crowded category, you just need a smarter angle:

They took the screen-time/productivity niche and turned it Christian: “Pray to unlock your apps”

It’s a genius way of targeting Gen Z/religious segment And they’re killing it at distribution, with at least 4 formats already proven viral:

1. Faceless bulk recorded – tt@prayscreenio, tt@pray.screen

“I can’t stop being tempted by sin” with p*rn background + guy throwing hand lotion away and grabbing the app

It’s weird, so it works: 226K views // 26K likes // 115 comments // 1070 saves

2. Faceless slideshows – A

“Facts about Christianity that make me sob” etc Most videos have zero to low views but this one went viral: 351K views // 82K likes // 258 comments // 14K saves

Text story telling in slideshows, whole account

One video reached 70K views, another 20K, the rest less

Bottom line,

– find a new angle to an already proven concept

– combine niches to find your own untapped one

– test, test, test

Their 3 most viral formats:

1) Open door & “catch” what tool they’re using Hooks – “She living in 2099”, “Where she find this”

They’re still struggling a bit to convert with in-app purchases ($3.99 for unlimited scans)

Bottom line,

– test formats and “steal” ideas from neighbor niches

article.content:
Garry Tan Turned YC’s YouTube Into a 70M-view media machine

How Garry Tan turned YC’s YouTube into a 70M-view media machine in just 2 years. i cannot believe every VC is sleeping o…

Garry Tan Turned YC’s YouTube Into a 70M-view media machine

How Garry Tan turned YC’s YouTube into a 70M-view media machine in just 2 years. i cannot believe every VC is sleeping o…

SGE Team

•

December 19, 2024

•

7 min read

Save for later

How Garry Tan turned YC’s YouTube into a 70M-view media machine in just 2 years.

i cannot believe every VC is sleeping on this:

The YC channel was launched 11 years ago with a video of Mark Zuckerberg at Startup School (yes, nothing less than that).

It took them 9 years to reach 40 million views.

Then Garry Tan took over. And in just 2-ish years,  almost doubled that:

But crazier, the number of subscribers went from 400k to 1.6M after Garry took over.

He has his own channel that has 8.5M views over 186 videos.

During the pandemic he had a strategy session with Mr Beast who told him:

Your “thumbnails and titles are garbage, they effing suck”

He was right.

The thumbnails and titles before:

The thumbnails and titles after:

The difference is astonishing.

And no, you cannot compare views like-for-like because the back catalog will continue to grow linearly (sometimes exponentially) as the channel expands.

This video from 5 years ago got 30% of its views just in the past year.

With the level of guests they have, they had a clear moat from the get-go.

But they only started capitalizing on it under Garry.

Since he’s a creator himself, he understands the codes and, having done it previously on his own channel, knew how to launch YC into today’s era of information consumption by the new generation.

He came up with incredible formats with Lightcone for instance. Great studio, and editing.

Even doing something as simple as a “coming up” with some highlights made a significant difference.

they’re also adding new formats like “Decoded,” on top of classics like “Startup School” and “Dalton & Michael.”

Plus, there are documentary-style episodes, like the one with Tom Blomfield—which is exceptionally cool:

They’re now competing in an increasingly professionalized title-and-thumbnail discovery feed.

Thankfully, they’re getting more kids to click on their quality content—and fewer to click on Alex Hormozi’s and other (worthless) gurus’ overly crafted thumbnails.

YC could definitely do way better with Shorts.

With the content quality they already have, they could easily turn each long video into at least two higher-quality, more dynamic Shorts by hiring skilled clippers/editors.

I recently met an agency that’s doing this for large channels and absolutely minting views.

These Shorts are generating tons of subscribers for the main channel, and you can link them to a video to funnel traffic from Shorts to long-form content.

For the long-form formats, every VC fund should take inspiration and do the same.

Hire someone dedicated to Thumbnails and Titles, and invest in producing higher-quality editing.

Capitalize on your founders and guests to start driving insane awareness:

Let’s take a look at how terrible some of these competing VC channels are.

1. Antler:

650 videos for 500K views. Average view count is embarrassing, as well as the Thumbnails’ (those colors…).

2. Sequoia:

Guests are mind-blowing. Titles, thumbnails and edits (and views) will make you want to burn the channel.

3. Techstars:

835 videos only 1.5M views

Thumbnails are just powerpoint covers. I wouldn’t click any of them, even under influence.

4. 500 Capital:

I mean…

5. a16z:

The Ben & Marc show performs well.

But with the level of guests, partners, and startups they have, they could be pulling in

immensely

more views.

That said, it used to be way worse.

Still, 1,054 videos for only 8M views?

There’s so much untapped potential.

VCs are boomers, but they’re targeting founders who are Gen Z and Alpha.

You see the issue – a clear mismatch in how they communicate and advertise.

Even ChatGPT knows…

Let’s be real… I’m paying my YT thumbnail guy $5 a pop (he’s doing an excellent job). And for the titles? A modest copywriter could whip up something exciting or click-baity without breaking the bank.

I cannot believe VCs are sleeping on this.

Building a back catalog of extremely valuable content is essentially free passive awareness for years—awareness that might one day nudge a deal toward their fund instead of someone else’s.

And if that lost deal turns out to be the next Uber or Perplexity, what’s the opportunity cost of not investing a modest amount of cash into building these media channels?

The future generation of startup founders will emerge from listening to creators like

@greg.isenberg

,

@garry.tan

,

@marc.lou

, and other YouTubers.

For example, my extremely bright 20-year-old brother consumes 95% of his content there. Most of his references come from “influencer”-led channels on the platform.

How to do it, step-by-step:

Offshore TikTok Faceless Scaling Last week I discovered an insane strategy where dozens of independent AI girlfriend app…

SGE Team

5 min read

Save for later

Offshore TikTok Faceless Scaling

Last week I discovered an

insane strategy

where dozens of independent AI girlfriend apps were running hundreds of faceless accounts, generating hundreds of millions of views.

In the end, I exposed that an agency was behind this scheme. Over 80 people DM’d me, asking for the name of this “agency.”

Does it just goes to show how crowded the AI girlfriend chatbot wrapper space has become?

and how crucial it is to master distribution in the ultra-competitive world of GPT/Llama-based chatbot wrappers.

We’ve seen similar strategies prove successful in other verticals, like

calorie-counting

apps.

The funny thing is, with just 15 minutes of research, anyone could find the name of this agency. The reality is that, because they don’t post in the US but rather from the Philippines and Georgia the strategy itself is simple to replicate.

Find the lowest-cost labor in the Philippines, Eastern Europe, or Asia (Fiverrr…)

Negotiate local fixed rates or fixed + CPM contracts

Analyze the top-performing videos from

Dippy

,

Crushon

& co

Build a library of pre-made assets to help with fast editing

Build a library of hooks / storylines

Make detailed guidelines on how to run & interact

Have them post 3 to 5 times a day on each account

Copy, iterate, and scale

Start with 4 or 5 accounts and, if there’s any success, scale to 100.

Even better, you could probably find one Filipino editor who cranks out hundreds of these videos daily while also managing dozens of posters for you.

And truly outsource directly to the source.

For the hooks

For each new vertical/approach, write 10 to 20 different ones based on previous insights or competitor/viral analysis.

After that, use Claude/GPT to create more variations.

After posting, once you’ve identified the winning hook categories, fine-tune and repeat with the hooks that generate the most views.

Alternatively, since these are faceless accounts, you could also have the content edited offshore or programmatically (still hard today, tbh) created and then use a phone farm in the U.S. for posting.

You can ramp up to 3 or 4 accounts per phone over a few weeks.

The hard part is ensuring the posting of so many videos. In the phone farm case, you’ll need an intern or someone dedicated in-house (or a more advanced automated system).

Or alternatively, you ditch the phone farm and get the cheapest labour – youngsters, else – to post from the US and incentivize them on a CPM outcome to make them scale for you (like an affiliates network).

If centralized, you need to ensure you identify the winners and interact with the comment sections.

Now the question is:

If everyone starts copying this strategy, will it saturate, or is there a near-infinite upside?

One thing to note is that these fast-food-like distribution models favor high volume with repeated retargeting.

Onshore / Offshore Content

I talked to someone last week who’s scaling a YouTube Shorts clipping enterprise through a mix of on-shore script building and off-shore editing.

Everyone in the content pipeline is incentivized based on CPM. A lot of this can be applied across strategies and platforms to optimize costs, reduce the cost per video, and improve target CPM ratios.

At scale, it becomes an operational cost machine.

So how do you reduce the cost per video & posting?

With a few companies we work with, we handle things like faceless bulk content generation offshore, while managing operators posting in the U.S. This drastically reduces costs.

It works well with faceless content, but even faceful content like:

…can be outsourced.

You only need the face recordings to be done offshore, and the text overlays and posting can be handled from anywhere.

By doing this, you can access “talent” with the most audience-relevant faces at a really low or reasonable price.

There are so many interesting approaches to mass content production.

As you scale volume, reducing your cost per video is the name of the game.

That said, scaling before you’ve locked in a working strategy is never a good idea.

In most instances, starting with 4 to 5 accounts posting 3x a day is enough to test various multi-account, mass-content formats.

What works repeatedly at a small scale will likely work repeatedly at a large scale.

A Newspaper For Organic Growth Marketing

Could be the most logical work of my career. After years of being in growth marketing, we’re now compiling all the organic growth strategies we’ve uncovered.

Since launching 3 weeks ago, it’s been read by more than 3,000 people. And 100+ people are tuning in, worldwide, every single day.

Last week, we gave it a lift and we’ve added a new section with actionable “How-to” information.

How to Warm up Accounts

How to Target the US with a new TikTok Account

How to Best Manage Content Performance

[…]

Those will be consistently updated.

This is just the beginning.

More and more useful insights will be added along with more growth-hacking analysis.

Everything for free.

When I started working in growth, I used to read the growthHackers(dot)com (now defunct) forum every day.

I want to recreate that feeling i had getting incredible growth ideas and insights every day.

If you haven’t, go check it out:

https://www.socialgrowthengineers.com/

Recently came across this “Call Santa” app that has been around for 10 years and did $100K MRR last month (600K downloads).

Seasonality is not necessarily bad thing for your app, if you get it done right.

They post throughout the whole year to keep accounts active and running, and then they double down in posting frequency right after Halloween.

They have one main account on TikTok & 7+ on Instagram (one per country). They also do some micro-influencer partnerships with parenting creators.

Their best performing videos feature the screen-recording of app call plus the reaction of the kids.

Dippy AI: 60+ accounts & 60M+ views in 3 month

Crushon AI: 50+ accounts & 80M+ views & $200K MRR app

11 different AI girlfriend apps are doing the exact same mass faceless TikTok growth hack (huge alpha):

I’ve been keeping an eye on how those AI “companionship” websites/apps that have been growing for a while now.

I knew they had a TikTok organic growth strategy but couldn’t find it,

Then I hit the jackpot. I discovered hundreds of accounts, active and posting daily – belonging to:

Dippy AI, Crushon AI, Talkie AI, Moemate AI, Juicy Chat AI, Alice AI, HeyReal AI, DokiChat AI, Sekay AI, TaleTape AI, and Onnichat AI:

They’re all using the same organic tiktok growth strategy, but they’re connected in any way.

Dippy AI is the biggest doing it right now, with 80+ accounts posting this faceless content:

@sabrinalolakawai

Dippy AI burns me A LOT of calories❤️????

#dippyai

#dippyapp

#dippyaichat

#dippyaibot

#artificialintelligence

#characterai

#booktiktok

#aibot

#characteraibot

#cai

#chatgpt

#anime

#characteraichat

#creatorsearchinsight

#creator

#fyp

#paradoxaai

♬ Apt – leonzickey

One core format they use consistently is the “Character AI vs. Dippy AI” comparison.

Each account is posting 3 times a day, featuring various types of videos.

100 videos a day total for Dippy.

The formats are similar but not entirely uniform. Other types of formats they’re using include:

It’s a large-scale growth scheme.

If you want to truly grasp the scale, check out all of Dippy’s accounts and stats in this collection (free):

https://app.shortimize.com/c/2a10VSrWYuy03z

When we found this, we thought they were either:

Programmatically created and posted using dozens of pre-made templates (though I doubt we’re at that level yet)

More likely, produced in bulk offshore, possibly in the Philippines or another country

The big question is how these accounts are being operated.

Our initial thought was that it was programmatic posting.

Judging by the comment section engagement and the variety of content, it seems these accounts are actually operated by humans:

Quantity/variety is just too large for it to be fully automated.

Looking at a sample of 10 accs, I found:

6 from the Philippines

4 from Georgia

Content is created & posted offshore by individuals and these are also responsible for interacting with comment section.

We assume they are paid based on a reward CPM$.

They’re operating offshore with high volume, which must allow them to target multiple countries simultaneously (including U.S. at a certain % rate)

What’s so interesting is this:

Crushon, Talkie, Moemate, Juicy Chat, Alice, HeyReaI, and DokiChat are all using the exact same strategy.

Crushon AI is doing it on the largest scale. Check out their accounts here:

https://app.shortimize.com/c/2a10CeXjTAT9YH

If you analyze their web traffic, you can clearly correlate their growth to when they started this strategy.

Traffic is from brand searches, which means it’s most likely driven by this TikTok scheme.

Side-by-side comparison of Dippy and Crushon:

Crushon AI is pulling in $300K MRR with their mobile app.

Moemate is doing $20K MRR with their app.

Juicy Chat is bringing in $10K MRR with their app.

Dippy just launched their app and is growing slowly, currently sitting at $15K MRR.

Two assumptions we wrestled with here: whether all these apps were owned by the same person or whether the same entity was behind the growth of all these apps:

We figured it out.

We found them. It’s two person/agency. They’re running the same growth hack and selling it to ALL these companionship apps.

They’re building a massive network of cheap labor in the Philippines and Georgia for editing, posting, and commenting.

Strategy must be wildly successful as they manage to sell it to almost every new app in this vertical.

At the start, when setting up a network of accounts, you need to monitor both each account’s individual health metrics a…

SGE Team

At the start, when setting up a network of accounts, you need to monitor both each account’s individual health metrics and the overall network health.

A good account — whether it has a 500 or 1K+ views median — shows high view variation. That means videos perform anywhere from 0.25x to 3x the median, and ideally, one video hits 5x to 10x the median every 5 to 10 days. That’s assuming the content you’re pushing is solid.

The idea behind horizontal scaling and multi-account marketing is to:

Give you a larger algorithm testing surface.

You’ll be able to push out way more videos each day, allowing you to test hooks, formats, and strategies at scale. Shooting 100 shots a day at the algorithm gives you a granular testing ground where you can almost scientifically run experiments.

Let you scale your reach aggressively.

You can’t scale your reach on a single account beyond what that account is capable of. You may hit limits on how many videos you can post per day.

A counterargument to point 2 could be: just increase video quality and you’ll get more views. That’s true, but eventually you still run into the same issue — even at higher quality, you don’t have the posting velocity needed to reach broader audiences. This matters less for top 5 creators who can cover a lot of ground with their core audience, but for anyone smaller, it applies.

Once your network is up and running, success can be measured by:

Total views and engagement generated daily or weekly

Frequency of 10x outliers

Number of 25x or 100x mega-viral outliers

The higher those numbers, the better.

You can track these metrics manually by reviewing each account (if you own them), or more efficiently by using tracking tools like

Shortimize

.

Attribution is a real challenge with TikTok and Reels organic marketing. Most conversions will come from direct brand se…

Save for later

Attribution is a real challenge with TikTok and Reels organic marketing.

Most conversions will come from direct brand searches, organic searches, or app store brand searches.

While you can attribute spikes in traffic to viral videos, it’s difficult to track consistent traffic from regular posting, especially when running multiple distribution channels simultaneously.

A few partial solutions:

1. Custom Domain:

For web apps, create a dedicated domain exclusively for TikTok/Reels. If you direct traffic to [yourdomain].ai instead of [yourdomain].com and ensure only this channel uses that domain, voilà—you’ve captured most of the “direct” clicks. Organic search might still default to your primary domain ranking higher, though.

2. Link in Bio:

Only captures a minor percentage of traffic but can serve as an indicator of growth and engagement trends.

3. Referral Codes:

These often feel promotional rather than authentically organic, slightly lowering conversion rates. Plus, only a fraction of viewers will actually use them.

4. Ad CPM vs. Organic CPM:

Calculating CPM through paid ads or regular influencer marketing provides a useful benchmark. It helps you estimate the number of organic views you’d need to match or surpass your paid CPM.

5. Traffic Source Differential:

If your app or site is established with clear traffic splits (direct, search, paid, social), measure your compounding growth in direct and organic searches. Analyzing these shifts will help pinpoint the impact of your TikTok or short-form video efforts.

With dedicated creators (ambassadors)

Some effective payment structures split fees into 50 % upfront and 50 % upon completion, or, alternatively, 25 % in advance with 25 % at set milestones.

For dedicated creators, we settle payment weekly and upfront, which unlocks the next batch of videos, with bonuses paid at the end of each cycle or month.

This approach increases trust and transparency for the creator while still protecting you from problems down the line.

If you already have a strong, trusting relationship, you can simply pay after the videos are posted.

With micro creators

When working with micro creators on a fixed fee, payment is usually issued after the demo is approved and before the video goes live.

If a CPM or milestone‑based reward system is in place, settle those payouts afterwards.

Contracts

Keep contracts short and clear.

Accept a range of payment methods, including PayPal, Stripe, and direct transfer. For younger creators, you can also offer Shein, Roblox, or Amazon vouchers.

Before signing a full contract with ambassadors or dedicated accounts, run test or demo videos to confirm that the content style and quality match your needs; this step ensures the creator can deliver.

For ambassador deals, make sure the contract includes a clause allowing the content to be boosted or reused for ads at your discretion. You can negotiate the same right with one‑off creator campaigns, but expect a higher rate.

What Should I do if My Account Gets Shadowbanned?

If you’re shadowbanned on a new account, there are two scenarios: Scenario 1: Your first video(s) get 0 views. In this c…

SGE Team

December 1, 2024

2 min read

Save for later

If you’re shadowbanned on a new account, there are two scenarios:

Scenario 1

: Your first video(s) get 0 views. In this case, keep posting for a few days — you might start getting distribution. If you don’t, go ahead and re-create an account.

Scenario

2

: Your videos get less than 150 views and usually only 1 like max. In this case, you could either be restricted for one reason or another, or your content just isn’t good enough. To fix the former, re-create an account on the same device or, ideally, on another device. For the latter, create a couple more accounts on different devices and test your content there. After posting on a handful of accounts, you’ll reduce statistical errors.

If you’re being shadowbanned on an existing account, keep posting but reduce your usual posting volume.

Another way to confirm a shadowban is if most of your views are coming exclusively from followers rather than a broader audience. Instead of deleting content, privatize it to avoid further penalties.

Accounts can take anywhere from 24 hours to 2 weeks to recover, and consistent posting is essential for restoring normal viewership.

For newer accounts, starting fresh may be the better option if recovery proves difficult.

During the recovery period, make sure you’re using only one account per device to avoid further complications.

Most bulk faceless content creators programmatically generate content using open-source libraries like MoviePy.

If you’re looking to convert long-form content into short-form, tools like Klap and others are a better option.

“AI” short-form generation SaaS tools are generally low quality and not recommended. Although they’re improving fast, the formats they unlock might be too restrictive or too competitive.

For carousels:

Download Pinterest images or GPT-4o images and create lines of carousels in Figma. Make them in bulk, repeat hooks. This is ideal for both hook/format testing and scaling a working strategy.

For videos:

Clipping

: Clipping is the process of chopping and remixing existing content. Through this process, you can make a nearly infinite number of videos. The best route is usually to either hire an army of clippers/posters or bring on a full-time editor. You’ll provide them with a bank of video assets and guidelines on how to create “viral” content.

Repurposing

: Repurposing content from other platforms, or your own content into different localities, can be a huge hack to increase output volume.

Programmatic

: This is often a mix between clipping and repurposing. Programmatically creating bulk video content — either through animated images, AI, or AI avatars — is a powerful way to scale aggressively. That said, this technique should only be used after finding content-market-fit.

The general consensus is that you can safely manage up to five accounts on a single device.

However, be cautious about creating them all at once. For safety, it’s recommended to space out the creation of new accounts by several days, if not weeks. Make sure each account is fully warmed up and actively running before creating the next one.

Ultimately, the fewer accounts you manage per phone, the better.

That said, there’s no official guide or definitive material on this topic, so it’s best to experiment and see what works for you.

We’ve worked with people who run 5+ accounts per device successfully, but we’ve also seen many try to create more accounts only to have them instantly restricted.

Scaling the number of phones is the safest route. Once your first account is solid and running, create another account on a new device.

Creator pricing can vary widely based on multiple factors.

Full-Time Gigs

There are four common ways to pay creators for full-time U.S.-based roles:

1. Full Fixed Retainer

Depending on the quality of the creator and the type of videos you’re after, costs can range from $250 to $5,000+/month.

For creators with experience in viral videos and a solid UGC (User-Generated Content) portfolio, expect to pay between $1,000 and $2,500.

For new creators or random individuals, you can aim for a lower range of $750 to $1,500.

2. Performance-Based Compensation

Using metrics like $1 CPM (Cost Per Mille, or cost per 1,000 impressions) can be highly cost-effective.

$1 CPM works well for broad audiences.

For highly targeted niches, you can aim for $2 to $5 CPM.

3. Part Retainer / Part Performance

This hybrid model is the most common. It combines a lower fixed retainer with performance-based or milestone-based incentives.

4. Affiliate-Only Payment

This model strictly incentivizes creators based on conversions, meaning you only pay for tangible results.

Keep in mind:

A

CPM model

protects you upfront if performance is low, but can become more expensive over time as the creator starts getting more views.

A

fixed retainer

is more expensive short term (since CPM is higher early on), but becomes extremely cost-effective once your strategy works and you’re generating millions of views at a low CPM.

Each of these models has its pros and cons and should be chosen based on your goals, industry, and situation.ality. You can use any of the payment methods mentioned above to structure deals effectively.

New TikTok accounts are distributed based on the phone’s current location. If you’re located in the U.S., your traffic will primarily come from the U.S. If you’re in France, the traffic will be in France.

If you travel to Morocco with a new account, your content will be distributed locally, within Morocco.

Over time, if you consistently speak and caption in your target language, you should start to see a gradual shift in distribution toward countries that match that language.

For example, if I post videos from Portugal in Portuguese, I might get distributed mostly in Brazil, since the audience size is larger there.

When a post gains traction, it will be distributed across your target country, but can also reach other locations. We’ve seen posts go viral on a U.S.-based phone and get major traffic from the U.K. and Europe.

While TikTok’s system is mostly a black box, there are some (limited) ways to predict where your content will be distributed.

Warming up accounts might or might not be necessary.

It hasn’t been scientifically proven.

Sometimes you can create a brand new account, post right away, and your content gets pushed out. Other times, the account might get shadowbanned.

It’s hard to say exactly

how

or

why

that happens.

Truth is, I wouldn’t risk it.

Just in case.

I do think warming up has some impact. At the very least, it helps reduce the chances of being flagged.

So, once you’ve set up your new account, follow these steps:

If you’ve got creators or third-party folks handling these accounts

, ask them to collect a list of 30 to 50 profiles within the niche you’re targeting.

Slowly start following those accounts and interacting with their content.

(Here’s an example of what a warm-up list looks like: [insert link])

Spend 15 minutes on the FYP

—scrolling through content

every day for 2 to 3 days

.

Only engage with content

within your niche

. Like, comment, bookmark—stay relevant.

During these first few days, set up your

bio

, add a

profile picture

, leave comments, and follow niche-relevant accounts.

Basically,

look, act, and behave like a real user

.

After 2 to 3 days of this warm-up phase, you can start posting.

Bonus tip:

Before and after you post, spend

2 to 3 minutes scrolling

on the FYP. This helps signal to the algorithm that you’re real… not just some spammy bot.

Their recruiting strategy:

https://www.instagram.com/sush_app/reel/DA6I2Wnx22o

Videos on TikTok and Instagram Reels calling for creators

Partnering with schools and universities (Syracuse, Empire State, etc.)

Even the brand’s main ambassador is a student working part-time for SUSH.

What they are offering:

$500 per month for posting three times per week (Monday to Friday), which amounts to $40 per video

Plus a $1,000 bonus per video that gets over 1 million views organically

So far, they have seven ambassador accounts running right now.

Four videos have gone viral (three by TikTok @sush.bernie and one by TikTok @sush.mo).

@sush.bernie

Its called SUSH!

#sushapp

♬ original sound – Jerry

So with only two accounts, they have achieved 20.8 million views in August and September (it appears that some of those views are from Spark Ads).

You can see all SUSH Ambassador accounts for free on the Shortimize public collection below.

Here is what I would do next if I were running this program:

Expand in the U.S., then by region

Expand in the U.S. quickly, then in a few months, they should expand to match their international multi-account strategy, as their Latin American accounts are working really well already.

Lower the cost per video

Once you have a solid creator network, it makes sense to figure out how to lower the cost per video and increase volume.

Learn from viral content and iterate

Get specific on what makes videos go viral and use that to upgrade their resource library and guidelines. High-performing creators could even be paid extra money to mentor newcomers.
